subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Rotary Engine
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Rotary Engine.

hook.text: Felix Wankel dreamed of an engine with no pistons—just a triangular rotor spinning inside an oval.

buildup.text: The rotor sweeps through intake, compression, power, and exhaust in one smooth rotation.

discovery.text: Mazda was the only brand to mass-produce rotary cars, starting with the Cosmo Sport in 1967.

twist.text: Rotaries are tiny and powerful but burn oil by design and guzzle fuel compared to piston engines.

climax.text: Mazda's RX-7 became a cult legend, but emissions rules eventually killed the rotary for road cars.

punchline.text: The engine without pistons won hearts but lost the emissions war.

quiz.question: Which company successfully mass-produced rotary engines?

details.summary: The rotary or Wankel engine replaces pistons with a triangular rotor spinning inside an epitrochoid housing, producing smooth, high-revving power from a remarkably compact package, championed almost exclusively by Mazda.
details.whyItMatters: The rotary engine demonstrates that radically different solutions to the combustion problem exist. Mazda's persistence with the design shows how unique engineering philosophies can differentiate a brand.
takeaways: A triangular rotor replaces pistons and connecting rods entirely
The design is extremely compact relative to its power output
Sealing and fuel efficiency challenges limited widespread adoption

faq.question: Why did only Mazda persist with rotary engines?
faq.answer: Other manufacturers abandoned the rotary due to poor fuel economy, high emissions, and seal durability issues. Mazda invested decades solving these problems because the rotary's smoothness and compactness defined its brand identity.

faq.question: Is the rotary engine making a comeback?
faq.answer: Mazda uses a small rotary as a range-extender generator in the MX-30 R-EV. The engine's compact size and smooth operation make it ideal for this role, even if it no longer directly drives the wheels.
